land.text: Britain, where 'early in 407, possibly February, his fellows acclaimed him as emperor', then Gaul

predecessors.note: A usurpation against Honorius; the western-roman-empire dossier carries the matching losses (Britain 407, Hispania early 408, Gaul May 408).

land.text: Arles, where Constantine was besieged until Constantius 'arrived at Arles while Gerontius was outside the city'

successors.note: Only Arles passes from Constantine III to Honorius in September 411. Hispania had gone to Gerontius's Maximus in 409 and the rest of Gaul in early 411 (ledger); Honorius's general Constantius took that from Gerontius's army (western-roman-empire ledger, 411). Britain left Constantine in 409 and Armorica in 409; neither returned to Honorius; Britain has no successor state until the Brythons (from 410, when the brythons dossier takes Roman Britain).

capitals.name: Arles
capitals.note: 'By May 408 Constantine had captured Arles and made it his capital'. In 407 he was in Britain and then Gaul; the page names no seat.

rulers.name: Constantine III
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign 407-411'; recognised by Honorius as co-emperor in early 409; beheaded in August or September 411 and his head presented to Honorius on 18 September.

rulers.name: Constans II
rulers.title: co-emperor
rulers.note: Raised by his father to co-emperor 'around' 409; killed early in 411 by Gerontius's army.

correction.text: Britain as the Western Roman Empire held it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 407: 'In 407, Constantine took charge of the remaining troops in Britain' and 'was acclaimed emperor in early 407'; the Constantine III page has Britain at the start of 407, then Gaul, with no date for his crossing. Britain only is drawn. Neither page gives an area.

New keyframe, 408: Britain, Gaul and Hispania with Arles as capital: 'By May 408 Constantine had captured Arles and made it his capital'; the Western Roman Empire page: Constantine 'invaded Gaul in 407'. Hispania: 'Early in 408, he was sent with Gerontius into Hispania'; Constans 'established himself at Saragossa and rebuilt the civilian administration'; 'Constantine established control over Gaul and Hispania'. The extent is the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape in each region.

New keyframe, 409-410: Gaul only. Honorius 'recognised Constantine as co-emperor' in early 409; 'later that year the Bagaudae of Armorica' expelled his officials and the Britons 'rebelled and expelled his officials' (409 or 410, End of Roman rule in Britain). Hispania, his since early 408, went to Gerontius and his emperor Maximus in 409 ('They set up court at Tarraco').

correction.text: Arles and its surroundings under siege

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 411: the siege of Arles. Gerontius, who 'caught him [Constans] at Vienne, probably early in 411', 'then besieged Constantine in Arles'; the rest of Gaul left him before (ledger, early 411) and the Rhine troops 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant', Jovinus. 'In 411 Honorius appointed a new general, Constantius, who took the Army of Italy over the Alps into Gaul'; Constantine was beheaded in August or September 411.

region.text: Britain, whose 'remaining troops' Constantine took charge of

ledger.note: early 407: the army in Britain acclaims Constantine emperor. 'was acclaimed emperor in early 407'; 'early in 407, possibly February, his fellows acclaimed him as emperor'; the Britain page: 'In 407, Constantine took charge of the remaining troops in Britain'. The Rhine had been crossed on 31 December 406 (same page).

region.text: Hispania: 'Early in 408, he was sent with Gerontius into Hispania'; 'Constantine established control over Gaul and Hispania'

ledger.note: early 408: Constans takes Hispania for his father. 'Early in 408, he was sent with Gerontius into Hispania'; he 'established himself at Saragossa and rebuilt the civilian administration'; 'Constantine established control over Gaul and Hispania'. The year is the page's; the extent (all of Hispania in the 406 shape) is the reading, since the page names only Saragossa. Mirrors western-roman-empire's 408 loss.
May 408: Constantine III holds Gaul from Arles. 'By May 408 Constantine had captured Arles and made it his capital'; the Western Roman Empire page: 'who invaded Gaul in 407'.
May 408: the seat is Arles. 'captured Arles and made it his capital'.

region.text: Armorica: 'the Bagaudae of Armorica also expelled his officials'

ledger.note: 409: Armorica expels his officials. 'later that year the Bagaudae of Armorica' did the same as the Britons; the Fall page has Armorica 'controlled by Bagaudae' from 400.

region.text: Britain, where the Romans 'rebelled and expelled his officials'

ledger.note: 409 (or 410): Britain expels Constantine's magistrates. 'expelled Constantine's magistrates in 409 or 410' (Britain page); the Constantine III page follows 'defeated the Saxons in 409' with the revolt. Honorius sent 'a rescript to British communities in 410 telling them to look to their own defence'.

region.text: Hispania: 'Gerontius rebelled, proclaiming his client Maximus as emperor'; 'They set up court at Tarraco'

ledger.note: 409: Gerontius rebels and proclaims Maximus. 'In 409 Gerontius rebelled, proclaimed his client Maximus as emperor'; 'They set up court at Tarraco'. Constans was 'sent back to Hispania' in spring or summer 409 and in 410 'attempted to subdue Gerontius. He failed', returning to Arles in spring 410; 'in autumn 409 much of the barbarian force entered Hispania'. The page names the court at Tarraco but not the territory Maximus held, so all of Hispania is the reading (confidence 2, not 3). Counterpart needs a dossier (Gerontius's Maximus, 409-411).

region.text: Gaul except Armorica and Arles: 'Gerontius's army then marched on Arles and besieged Constantine'

ledger.note: early 411: Gerontius defeats Constans and besieges Constantine in Arles. 'Gerontius caught him at Vienne, probably early in 411, defeated his army and killed Constans'; 'Gerontius's army then marched on Arles and besieged Constantine'. The page names no territory Gerontius took; with Constantine shut up in Arles the rest of Gaul is drawn as lost to the Rhine army's new emperor Jovinus (the year is the page's, the extent the reading). The Rhine troops 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant to the imperial throne', Jovinus (411, no date within the year), who needs a dossier of his own. Repair fx-28: the counterpart was maximus-usurper, but the page names no territory Gerontius took and says only that the Rhine troops 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant to the imperial throne'; the Jovinus page has Jovinus 'proclaimed emperor at Mainz in 411' and holding Gaul 'for about two years', so the land goes to jovinus-usurper (Constantine keeps Arles to August-September 411). Opened: Constantine III and Jovinus pages.

August-September 411: Constantine III is beheaded. 'had him and Julian beheaded in either August or September 411'; 'His head was mounted on a pole and presented to Emperor Honorius on 18 September'; Honorius's general Constantius takes Arles; the rest of Gaul had passed to Gerontius's Maximus earlier in 411 (previous event). Jovinus's revolt in the Rhine army is 'suppressed' in 413.

wars.name: Revolt of Constantine III

zones.text: Hispania: Constans's from early 408, Gerontius's and Maximus's from 409

wars.outcome: Constantine held Britain from 407, Gaul and (through Constans) Hispania from 408, was recognised as co-emperor in early 409, lost Britain, Armorica and Hispania in 409, led an army into northern Italy in spring 410 and withdrew, lost the rest of Gaul to Gerontius's Maximus in early 411, and was beheaded in August or September 411 after Constantius's arrival at Arles.
wars.note: 'Early in 408, he was sent with Gerontius into Hispania'; 'In 409 Gerontius rebelled, proclaimed his client Maximus emperor'; Constans was killed 'probably early in 411'.

wars.name: Siege of Arles
wars.outcome: Gerontius and then Constantius besieged Constantine in Arles; he surrendered and was beheaded in August or September 411.

certainty.note: Provinces are named, not boundaries; the extent in Britain, Gaul and Hispania 407-410 is the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape in each region, and only Arles is certain in 411.

sources.title: Constantine III (Western Roman emperor)
sources.note: Acclamation in 407, Arles by May 408, the co-emperor recognition of early 409, Gerontius, Armorica, the 410 Italian expedition, the siege and death in 411.

sources.title: End of Roman rule in Britain
sources.note: 407 troops in Britain, expulsion of magistrates 409 or 410, the 410 rescript.

sources.title: Western Roman Empire
sources.note: 'invaded Gaul in 407'; Honorius defeated Gerontius and Maximus in 411 and executed Constantine III.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written because the western-roman-empire dossier's 407-411 losses need a counterpart. Cliopatria's Western Roman Empire 407 and 410 shapes drop Britain, Gaul or Spain to the Vandals instead (reviewed there). Extents are read from Cliopatria's 406 Western Roman Empire shape (Britain, Gaul and Hispania regions intersected with it) because the page gives no boundaries. Hispania IS in the realm from early 408 ('Constantine established control over Gaul and Hispania'; Constans at Saragossa) until Gerontius's revolt in 409; the first version of this dossier left it out, and the review corrected that. The realm shrinks in three steps: Britain and Armorica in 409, Hispania in 409 (to Gerontius's Maximus), Gaul except Arles in early 411 (Gerontius's army at Vienne and Arles). The two counterparts without a dossier are slug maximus-usurper (Gerontius's emperor Maximus, Hispania 409-411 and Gaul in 411; not Magnus Maximus of 383-388) and Jovinus (Rhine, 411-413). Disagreement with the reviewer: the 409 loss of Hispania is confidence 2, not 3, because the page names only the court at Tarraco and says nothing on the territory Maximus held. The Constantine III page gives no date for his crossing to Gaul, which the Western Roman Empire page puts in 407; 408 is used for the gain because of the dated Arles sentence. Neither page has an area. Wikidata id unknown. Page budget: shares the pages of the Western Roman Empire dossier.
